previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: Mr. Johnson was admitted with fever and chills two days after his chemotherapy infusion. Workup revealed elevated bilirubin and transaminitis, concerning for biliary obstruction and cholangitis. A CT scan showed persistent dilation of the right hepatic duct with functioning stents. He underwent ERCP, which confirmed sludge and stones in the right biliary stent, which were cleared. He was treated with IV antibiotics, transitioned to oral ciprofloxacin and metronidazole, and showed clinical improvement with normalization of liver function tests and resolution of fever. His hyponatremia resolved with hydration, and cytopenias were attributed to recent chemotherapy. He was discharged home on a 14-day antibiotic course with follow-up planned with oncology.

# E. Coli bacteremia: the patient was found to have e.coli 
bacteremia and was initially started on zosyn and transitioned 
to meropenem in house based on culture sensis. He was changed

admission which did not recur after he was started on broad

clear: UA, RUQ and CT abdomen and pelvis were negative. 
Possibly, a transient biliary obstruction lead to his 
bacteremia. He did not require ERCP during this admission.

was positive. Diarrhea improved with treatment with PO Vanco, 
with which he was treated due to his age and his concomitant 
bacteremia with aid from ID consultants. He should take PO vanco 
while he is being treated with ertapenem and for 2 weeks 
following completion of ertapenem, until ___.

His confusion improved with treatment, but he was still a bit

million and she stated that he was previously a shy, reserved 
man, and he is currently quite talkative. For these reasons, CT
